_comment: X-02 · The mock case dataset. Drives every prototype screen, and is shaped to the real contracts so phase 2 can adopt it as a test fixture unchanged. Fictional company; every number here is invented.

company.sector: Retail trade via mail order houses or internet

findings.title: Rejecting all cookies leaves 9 of 14 trackers running
findings.why: When someone refuses, the site keeps loading the same third parties it loads for someone who agreed. The refusal is recorded in your banner but never acted on, so nine companies still receive data about that visitor.

evidence.caption: Pass B (reject all) vs Pass C (accept all) — 9 hosts identical

remedy.title: Move the tags behind the consent state
remedy.detail: Your tags fire on page load rather than on the consent event. Wrap each non-essential tag in a consent check and re-publish. The snippet below is the pattern for the container you are using.

findings.title: You sell a service but publish no data processing agreement
findings.why: Your customers hand you their customers' personal data, which makes you their processor. They are required to have an agreement with you covering it, and right now there is nothing on your site for them to sign or accept.

citations.note: required content of a processor agreement

evidence.caption: /vilkaar and /handelsbetingelser fetched — no Article 28 terms found
lines: searched for: instruction · confidentiality · sub-processor · breach notification · deletion · audit

remedy.title: Generate your processing agreement and sub-processor page
remedy.detail: We can draft both from what this case already knows — your vendors, where they sit, and what they handle. You review, a named person signs, and it publishes to your own site.

findings.title: Contact form posts through an HTTP redirect before reaching TLS
findings.why: The form submits to an address that redirects. For the length of that first request the message and the sender's details travel unencrypted, which anyone on the same network can read.

evidence.caption: Observed on /kontakt
lines: form fields in the first request: navn, email, telefon, besked

remedy.title: Point the form at the https address and add HSTS
remedy.detail: Change the form action to the https address so nothing is sent over the redirect, then add the header below so browsers never try http again.

findings.title: Staff are pasting customer data into a US chat assistant
findings.why: You told us four people use it for customer correspondence. That sends customer names, addresses and order details to a processor you have no agreement with, in a country outside the EEA.

evidence.caption: From your own answer on 4 September
lines: Question: Do staff use AI assistants with customer data?
Answer: Yes — about 4 people, for writing customer replies

remedy.title: Move those four people to GDPR Chat
remedy.detail: Same experience your staff already know, hosted in the EU, with a processing agreement and no training on your content. This is our own product — we are telling you that plainly.
remedy.alternativeNote: There is no free fix for this one. If you would rather not use ours, we list three European alternatives.

findings.title: Mail and files sit with a US-parented provider
findings.why: Your mail and document storage are with a provider whose ultimate parent is established in the United States. European data residency does not change which courts can compel that parent, and your policy names no basis for the transfer.

evidence.caption: From your DNS records
lines: contracting entity: EU · ultimate parent: US

remedy.title: Compare European alternatives
remedy.detail: This is a choice with real trade-offs and switching cost. Three European-owned options we have checked, with what each would and would not solve.
options: Mailbox provider, DE — mail only, keeps your files where they are
Collaboration suite, FR — mail and files, migration tooling included
Collaboration suite, DE — mail and files, on-premise option

findings.title: Session replay records what people type on the checkout page
findings.why: A replay tool is active on the checkout with input masking switched off. It captures keystrokes as they are typed — including the address and card fields — before anyone presses submit.

evidence.caption: Observed on /kassen
lines: www.clarity.ms/tag/... loaded on pass A (before any consent)
fields in scope: navn, adresse, postnr, email, telefon, kortnummer

remedy.title: Turn masking on and exclude the checkout
remedy.detail: Two changes: mask all input by default, and stop the tool loading on the checkout path entirely. The second is the one that matters.

findings.title: Your privacy policy states no retention period for anything
findings.why: People are entitled to know how long you keep their data, for each purpose. Your policy describes what you collect and why, but never says for how long.

evidence.caption: /privatlivspolitik · 2,140 words · searched for a stated duration
lines: searched: opbevar* · slet* · periode · år · måneder · retention
nearest text: "Vi opbevarer dine oplysninger så længe det er nødvendigt."
that phrase is not a period

remedy.title: Rewrite the section from your register
remedy.detail: We need two things from you first — how long you keep orders, and how long you keep newsletter sign-ups. Then this section writes itself from your register rather than from a template.

findings.title: Web fonts load from a US endpoint, sending every visitor's IP address
findings.why: Two fonts are fetched from an external host on every page load. That transmits each visitor's IP address to a third party before they have agreed to anything, and a German court has awarded damages over exactly this.

evidence.caption: Four requests on pass A, before any interaction

remedy.title: Self-host the two fonts
remedy.detail: Download the two families, put them beside your stylesheet, and declare them locally. Nothing leaves your server and the page gets slightly faster.

findings.title: No mention of the right to complain to Datatilsynet
findings.why: Your policy lists most of the rights people have, but omits the right to lodge a complaint with the supervisory authority, which has to be stated.

evidence.caption: /privatlivspolitik · rights section
lines: present: indsigt · berigtigelse · sletning · begrænsning · dataportabilitet

remedy.title: Add the two missing paragraphs
remedy.detail: Two paragraphs, in Danish, naming the right authority for your country and the correct way to withdraw consent for your setup.

findings.title: Newsletter sign-up is bundled with accepting the terms
findings.why: One checkbox at checkout covers both agreeing to the terms and joining the newsletter. Consent to marketing has to be a separate, freely given choice.

evidence.caption: /kassen · single input covering two purposes
lines: label: "Jeg accepterer handelsbetingelserne og vil gerne modtage nyhedsbrevet"
required = true — the order cannot be placed without also joining

remedy.title: Split it into two checkboxes
remedy.detail: Terms stays required. The newsletter becomes a second, optional, unticked box. Your list gets smaller and considerably more valuable.
remedy.snippet:
<label><input type="checkbox" required> Jeg accepterer handelsbetingelserne</label>
<label><input type="checkbox"> Ja tak til nyhedsbrevet</label>

findings.title: No sub-processor list published
findings.why: Your own customers need to know who else touches their data through you, and to be told when that changes. We have already mapped 21 of them from your vendors' own documents.

evidence.caption: Supply chain mapped from published documents
lines: source: each vendor's own published list, dated

remedy.title: Publish the list we already built
remedy.detail: It stays current — when a vendor changes their own list, this case notices and tells you.

findings.title: One third-party host could not be identified
findings.why: Something on your site loads from a host we cannot trace to a company. We are not going to guess. Until someone identifies it, you cannot list it in your policy or your register, and neither can we.

evidence.caption: Unresolved after registry, WHOIS and certificate lookup
lines: registrar privacy service · no organisation on certificate
not present in our vendor registry

remedy.title: We have no good answer to this yet
remedy.detail: There is no reliable public way to attribute an anonymised CDN host. We have written this down with your sector and country. If it turns out that thousands of European companies have the same unanswerable question, that is what tells us to go and build something for it.
remedy.askLabel: Do you know what this is?

newInWatch.title: A new tracker appeared on the checkout page
newInWatch.why: Something added a tag to /kassen on Tuesday that was not there last week. It fires before any consent.

evidence.caption: Weekly watch · 11 Sep vs 4 Sep
lines: fires on pass A — before any interaction

remedy.title: Ask who added it, then gate it like the others
remedy.detail: This is the ordinary way compliance decays. Somebody in marketing added a pixel for a campaign. It needs the same consent gate as the rest.

steps.title: Make your cookie banner do what it says
steps.plain: Right now, clicking "reject" doesn't actually stop anything. Of everything on this list, this is the one that matters most.

steps.title: Fix two quick things on your forms
steps.plain: Your contact form sends details unencrypted for a moment, and the newsletter box is tied to accepting the terms. Both are small changes.

steps.title: Stop sending visitor details to servers you don't control
steps.plain: Two things on your site quietly hand data to other companies before anyone agrees to it — your fonts, and a tool that records what people type.

steps.title: Tell people what they're entitled to
steps.plain: Your privacy policy is missing two short paragraphs. We've written them — you just need to read them and say yes.

steps.title: Answer four questions about how you work
steps.plain: Four things we can't see from outside. Each one is a single tap, and you can always say "check it for me" instead.
steps.invite: Two of these belong to IT — you can pass them on

steps.title: Publish the three documents you're missing
steps.plain: We write them from your answers, so they describe what you actually do. Someone with authority reads and signs, then they go live on your site.

steps.title: Two decisions only you can make
steps.plain: These aren't tasks with a right answer — they're choices about cost and convenience. We'll lay out the options and you decide.

watchStep.title: Something changed on your site
watchStep.plain: Someone added a tracking tag to your checkout page on Tuesday. This is normal — it's why we keep looking every week.

undetermined.title: Whether your policy names a legal basis for marketing
undetermined.reason: The section describes marketing but the wording is ambiguous about whether it relies on consent or on legitimate interests. We will not guess which — the answer changes what you have to offer people.
undetermined.resolve: One question, or a lawyer's eye

undetermined.title: Whether old customer records are actually deleted
undetermined.reason: Nothing a visitor's browser can see would tell us. It needs either an answer from you or a look at the system.
undetermined.resolve: Ask IT, or connect the system read-only

Rights paragraphs added to the policy

Staff moved to an EU assistant

questions.text: You run Microsoft 365. Do your customer files sit in SharePoint or OneDrive?
questions.why: It decides whether your file storage belongs in the register as a separate processing activity, and whether the transfer question applies to files as well as mail.

questions.text: Do staff use AI assistants with customer data?
questions.why: If yes, that is a processor you almost certainly have no agreement with, and it is usually outside the EEA.

questions.text: How long do you keep customer orders after the last purchase?
questions.why: Your policy has to state a period, and Danish bookkeeping law sets a floor you cannot go below. We will reconcile the two.
options: As long as the account exists

questions.text: Who should receive requests from people asking for their data?
questions.why: You need a named route with a one-month clock. Right now requests would arrive at a shared inbox nobody owns.

items.text: Confirm which tracking tools are still in use
Fix the reject path so refusing actually refuses
Separate the newsletter opt-in at checkout
Confirm the 14 services we found in your DNS records

Set a deletion job for orders older than the retention period
Approve the staff privacy notice we drafted
Set how long job applications are kept
Flag any staff monitoring tools in use
Confirm which vendors you have a signed agreement with
Review and sign the processing agreement
Resolve the bookkeeping vs erasure conflict

Personnel bound to confidentiality; measures listed by reference to the current state of the case, including the two items still open.

signoff.note: A named person has to sign this before it can be published. This is not legal advice — have your lawyer read it.
